payload.problem_statement: High-speed railway embankments built on weak soil foundations experience long-term settlement that can exceed design tolerances, causing track geometry deviations, speed restrictions, and structural failure. Current practice relies on static pre-construction calculations (PLAXIS FEM) and periodic surveys that cannot detect accelerating consolidation between intervals. There is no continuous digital twin for real-time comparison of observed vs predicted settlement in shadow mode alongside approved calculations.
payload.observed_context: No existing GeoSophia codebase or artifacts found in workspace project 35. A previous discovery document (discovery-34.md) covers a closely related concept for general railway embankments and was recommended as 'clarify'. This episode adds the high-speed rail (ВСЖД) dimension with tighter tolerances. The saga-mcp repository contains the Saga 3 framework, unrelated to geotechnical engineering.
assumptions: Instrumentation data is available at monitoring points during and after construction
PLAXIS model parameters can be extracted or manually entered into the system
A simplified 1D consolidation model provides sufficient accuracy for early-warning divergence detection on ВСЖД embankments
Stakeholders accept a shadow-mode product that advises but does not replace regulatory calculations per SNiP/GOST
Internet connectivity exists at construction sites, or edge devices can buffer and sync periodically
unknowns: Specific instrumentation standards and data formats used by Russian high-speed railway projects (RZD GOST vs international)
Whether PLAXIS models can be exported in a machine-readable format preserving layer parameters and boundary conditions
Regulatory requirements for settlement monitoring documentation on ВСЖД in Russia — whether shadow system outputs have recognized supplementary value
Typical data frequency from instrumentation (hourly, daily, event-triggered)
Existing commercial solutions setting market expectations in the Russian market
Target deployment model: cloud SaaS, on-premise, or hybrid edge-cloud
Relationship to epic 34 — refinement, continuation, or separate initiative
risks: 1D consolidation models may produce false positives/negatives in complex geological conditions
Railway safety regulations (SNiP, GOST) may not recognize shadow-system outputs; engineers reluctant to act on non-certified warnings
Geotechnical engineers are conservative; convincing them requires rigorous validation against known case studies
Instrumentation failures produce gaps or outliers requiring graceful handling without false alerts
PLAXIS has limited API; manual parameter entry introduces transcription errors
Russian high-speed rail market is small; product may need international markets to achieve scale
payload.candidate_scope: A shadow-mode settlement risk monitoring service for high-speed rail embankments that: (1) ingests time-series data from instrumentation via OPC-UA/Modbus/CSV, (2) maintains a 1D Terzaghi consolidation model calibrated to approved PLAXIS parameters per monitoring point, (3) computes real-time divergence with configurable ВСЖД-specific alert thresholds, (4) produces risk dashboard with per-point status and PDF reports, (5) operates strictly in shadow mode with advisory-only disclaimers. Out of scope: 2D/3D FEM re-analysis, automated design recalculation, SCADA integration.
evidence_refs: Task description from Saga MCP task 6251
Domain knowledge: Terzaghi 1D consolidation theory, PLAXIS FEM software, ВСЖД track geometry tolerances
payload.rationale: The idea addresses a genuine gap in high-speed railway embankment monitoring — continuous shadow-mode comparison of observed vs predicted settlement with ВСЖД-specific tolerances. However, critical unknowns must be resolved: (1) relationship to epic 34 which covered a nearly identical concept, (2) Russian ВСЖД regulatory landscape for supplementary monitoring outputs, (3) data availability and formats in target projects, (4) PLAXIS integration path, (5) market sizing given the limited Russian high-speed rail segment. The core concept is sound but requires targeted clarification before formalization.
